title: Keep the trusted statement in a Mathlib-only challenge file
problem: A huge proof (hundreds of files) must be checked against a statement that a reader can audit in one screen, without trusting any of the project files.
method_md: openai/math puts every headline statement in `ComparatorChallenges/<Name>.lean`: it imports only `Mathlib`, contains the minimal definitions the statement needs and ends in `sorry`. A sibling `<Name>.json` names the `challenge_module`, the `solution_module`, the `theorem_names` (and, rarely, `definition_names` for witnesses that must also match), and `permitted_axioms` = `propext`, `Quot.sound`, `Classical.choice`. The Comparator tool (with `lean4export`) then checks that the solution environment contains the same declarations with the same types and only those axioms. Each result also gets `docs/NNN.md` with a plain *Scope* section that says what is formalised and, explicitly, what "remains unformalized"; `formalization.yaml` catalogues 225 main results. For nosorry this is the same discipline as the problem statement: write the target exactly once, copy it verbatim into the proof file, and treat any difference as a failure, not a detail.

-- ComparatorChallenges/MatrixExponent.lean (shape)
import Mathlib
namespace OAI.LinearAlgebra.SpectralBooks
-- ... minimal definitions: Gate, Program, FormalCorrect, formalOmega ...
theorem square_exponent (F : Type*) [Field F] : formalOmega F 1 1 1 = (9 : ℝ) / 4 := by
  sorry
end OAI.LinearAlgebra.SpectralBooks

title: Re-declare the statement definitions verbatim, same names and namespaces
problem: The proof development has its own richer definitions, but the checker compares the statement against the challenge declaration by declaration; a renamed namespace or reordered field makes the statements different.
method_md: In openai/math the solution side copies the challenge definitions character for character under the same fully qualified names (the Sidorenko solution starts with a `Basic.lean` that repeats `faces`, `incidence`, `H`, `homCount`, `homDensity` exactly; the matrix-exponent solution keeps `OAI.MatrixMultiplication.Arithmetic.Gate`/`Program` and `SpectralBooks.formalOmega` with identical bodies). Only after that does it prove the equivalence with its working definitions. The history file records a real failure of this rule: for the CM Hodge result "diverging namespaces in the Comparator challenge and solution were adjusted". In a nosorry submission the same applies: paste the problem statement and its auxiliary `def`s unchanged, do not "tidy" binder names, implicit arguments or the order of conjuncts, and put your own helper definitions under different names.

title: Prove the statement model equivalent to your working model, then transport
problem: The statement uses a model convenient to read (e.g. a gate table or a division-free program), while the proof is far easier in another model (a set-valued build relation, circuits with division, tensor rank).
method_md: openai/math never proves the headline theorem directly in the statement model. For VP vs VNP the file `Valiant/Project.lean` proves `isVP_iff : Project.IsVP p ↔ VPVNP.IsVP p` and `isVNP_iff` (the latter just reuses the former on the verifier), and the final theorem is a three-line transport through `funext`/`propext`. For ω the challenge counts division-free programs with formal polynomial semantics, the internal `MatrixExponent.omega` uses a `Build` relation on the rational function field with division allowed; `formalOmega_square_eq_omega` closes the gap via tensor rank (`square_rank_iff` swaps the last two tensor indices to match the two rank conventions). Put each bridge in its own small file named after the model pair; it isolates the statement-specific bookkeeping from the mathematics and makes a later change of statement cheap.

theorem isVP_iff (p : Family F σ) : IsVP p ↔ VPVNP.IsVP p := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hfamily, s, hs, h⟩
    refine ⟨hfamily, VPVNP.PolynomiallyBounded.of_le hs fun n => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := computes_iff.mp (h n)
    exact hc ▸ VPVNP.circuitSize_le_of_circuit c
  · rintro ⟨hfamily, hsize⟩
    exact ⟨hfamily, fun n => VPVNP.circuitSize (p n), hsize,
      fun n => computes_iff.mpr (VPVNP.circuitSize_spec (p n))⟩

theorem vp_ne_vnp (F : Type u) [Field F] :
    (Valiant.Project.IsVP : Valiant.Project.Family F (fun n => Fin n × Bool) → Prop) ≠
      Valiant.Project.IsVNP := by
  intro same
  apply VPVNP.vp_ne_vnp F
  funext f
  apply propext
  exact (Valiant.Project.isVP_iff f).symm.trans ((Iff.of_eq (congrFun same f)).trans
    (Valiant.Project.isVNP_iff f))

title: Model straight-line programs as an inductive indexed by register count
problem: Arithmetic circuits need a cost, a semantics and reuse of earlier values; ad hoc lists of gates make every gate reference a proof obligation.
method_md: The ω statement uses `Gate F Input Register` (constant, input, add, sub, mul) and `Program F Input r` with `step : Program F Input r → Gate F Input (Fin r) → Program F Input (r+1)`: each new gate may only read the `r` existing registers, so well-formedness is by typing. Cost and semantics are structural recursions; the semantics `registerPolynomial` maps a program to `Fin r → MvPolynomial I F` with `Fin.cases`, so the newest register is index `0`, and the two `rfl` lemmas `registerPolynomial_zero`/`_succ` are tagged `@[simp]`. Constants and inputs cost 0, so the cost counts exactly the binary operations. The VP statement uses the alternative "table" form (`Computes s p : ∃ v : Fin s → MvPolynomial σ F, …` with an `available k` predicate); both forms avoid any graph or DAG library.
lean:
inductive Gate (F Input Register : Type*) where
  | constant : F → Gate F Input Register
  | input : Input → Gate F Input Register
  | add : Register → Register → Gate F Input Register
  | sub : Register → Register → Gate F Input Register
  | mul : Register → Register → Gate F Input Register

inductive Program (F Input : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | nil : Program F Input 0
  | step {r : ℕ} : Program F Input r → Gate F Input (Fin r) → Program F Input (r + 1)

def gatePolynomial [CommRing F] (g : Gate F I R) (v : R → MvPolynomial I F) :
    MvPolynomial I F :=
  g.casesOn (fun c => MvPolynomial.C c) (fun i => MvPolynomial.X i)
    (fun i j => v i + v j) (fun i j => v i - v j) (fun i j => v i * v j)

def registerPolynomial [CommRing F] : {r : ℕ} → Program F I r → Fin r → MvPolynomial I F
  | _, .nil => Fin.elim0
  | _, .step p g => Fin.cases (gatePolynomial g (registerPolynomial p)) (registerPolynomial p)

@[simp] theorem registerPolynomial_zero [CommRing F] {r : ℕ} (p : Program F I r)
    (g : Gate F I (Fin r)) :
    registerPolynomial (p.step g) 0 = gatePolynomial g (registerPolynomial p) := rfl

title: Demand formal polynomial identities, not function equality, over finite fields
problem: Over a finite field two different polynomials can define the same function (x^q = x on F_q), so "the circuit computes the product" is ambiguous and a function-level statement can be much weaker.
method_md: The ω statement defines correctness as equality in `MvPolynomial I F` (`FormalCorrect`), and the docs say so explicitly: "requires formal polynomial identities even over finite fields". The internal model works in `FractionRing (MvPolynomial (Var n) F)`, so a division gate tests `y ≠ 0` as a rational function, again independent of the size of `F` ("the division rule tests the denominator in the rational function field, even in positive characteristic"). When you read or write a statement about algebraic complexity, check which notion is used: `MvPolynomial.eval`-equality on all points of a finite field is strictly weaker, and a proof for one does not transfer to the other without `MvPolynomial.funext` (which needs an infinite field).
lean:
/-- Formal correctness, including over a finite ground field. -/
def FormalCorrect [CommRing F] {a b c : ℕ} (P : MatrixAlgorithm F a b c) : Prop :=
  ∀ i k, registerPolynomial P.program (P.output i k) =
    ∑ j : Fin b, MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inl (i, j)) * MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inr (j, k))

-- Internal model: values live in the field of rational functions.
abbrev Rat (F : Type*) [Field F] (n : ℕ) := FractionRing (MvPolynomial (Var n) F)

inductive Build {K : Type*} [Field K] (S : Set K) : ℕ → Set K → Prop
  | nil : Build S 0 S
  | add {m T x y} : Build S m T → x ∈ T → y ∈ T → Build S (m + 1) (insert (x + y) T)
  | mul {m T x y} : Build S m T → x ∈ T → y ∈ T → Build S (m + 1) (insert (x * y) T)
  | div {m T x y} : Build S m T → x ∈ T → y ∈ T → y ≠ 0 → Build S (m + 1) (insert (x / y) T)

title: Define exponents as sInf with ε-slack so the infimum is itself admissible
problem: Exponents like ω are infima of admissible exponents; working with `sInf` on ℝ is painful (it is 0 on the empty set and on unbounded-below sets) and the infimum is usually not attained.
method_md: Make admissibility already carry an ε: `Admissible τ := ∀ ε > 0, ∃ C > 0, ∀ N ≥ 1, cost N ≤ C * N^(τ+ε)`. Then (1) the set is nonempty as soon as one naive algorithm is admissible (here `formalAdmissibleExponent_naive` with constant 16), which is needed before any `csInf` lemma; (2) the infimum is admissible: given ε, pick τ < sInf + ε/2 in the set with `exists_lt_of_csInf_lt`, use its ε/2 bound and monotonicity of `rpow` in the exponent. Lower bounds `load ≤ τ` for every admissible τ give `≤ sInf` by `le_csInf`; upper bounds come from a single admissible witness and `csInf_le` (bounded below by the lower bound). Keep the "nonempty" and "bounded below" facts as named lemmas; without them `sInf` silently returns 0 and goals become false.
lean:
theorem formalOmega_admissible (F : Type*) [Field F] {w12 w23 w31 : ℝ}
    (h12 : 0 ≤ w12) (h23 : 0 ≤ w23) (h31 : 0 ≤ w31) :
    FormalAdmissibleExponent F w12 w23 w31 (formalOmega F w12 w23 w31) := by
  intro ε hε
  let S := {τ : ℝ | FormalAdmissibleExponent F w12 w23 w31 τ}
  have hS : S.Nonempty := ⟨_, formalAdmissibleExponent_naive F h12 h23 h31⟩
  obtain ⟨τ, hτ, hclose⟩ := exists_lt_of_csInf_lt hS
    (lt_add_of_pos_right (sInf S) (half_pos hε))
  obtain ⟨C, hC, hbound⟩ := hτ (ε / 2) (half_pos hε)
  refine ⟨C, hC, fun N hN => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨P, hP, hcost⟩ := hbound N hN
  refine ⟨P, hP, hcost.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ?_ hC.le)⟩
  apply Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le (by exact_mod_cast hN)
  change τ + ε / 2 ≤ sInf S + ε
  linarith

title: Turn a real-power threshold into a natural-number inequality
problem: Comparisons like `r < n ^ (9/4 : ℝ)` with `Real.rpow` resist `norm_num`/`decide`, yet the concrete cases are integer facts.
method_md: Raise both sides to the denominator of the exponent and cast back: `(r : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) ^ (9/4 : ℝ) ↔ r ^ 4 < n ^ 9`. The proof rewrites `(n ^ (9/4)) ^ 4 = n ^ 9` with `Real.rpow_mul_natCast`, uses `pow_lt_pow_iff_left₀` (both sides nonnegative) and finishes with `norm_cast`. After this one lemma every threshold test is a `Nat` inequality decidable by `decide`/`norm_num`, which the repo exploits in the prime-field reduction ("the threshold can be tested with integer arithmetic alone"). The same trick works for any rational exponent p/q.
lean:
theorem rank_threshold (n r : ℕ) :
    (r : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) ^ (9 / 4 : ℝ) ↔ r ^ 4 < n ^ 9 := by
  have he : ((n : ℝ) ^ (9 / 4 : ℝ)) ^ (4 : ℕ) = (n : ℝ) ^ (9 : ℕ) := by
    rw [← Real.rpow_mul_natCast (Nat.cast_nonneg n)]
    norm_num
  rw [← pow_lt_pow_iff_left₀ (Nat.cast_nonneg (α := ℝ) r)
    (Real.rpow_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg n) (9 / 4)) (by decide : (4 : ℕ) ≠ 0), he]
  norm_cast

title: Prove "for every field" via prime fields, extension invariance and a universe lift
problem: Statements quantify over `(F : Type*) [Field F]` in an arbitrary universe, but the proof only works for concrete fields (ZMod p, ℚ, algebraic closures).
method_md: First prove that the quantity is invariant under field extension (`omega_extension F K [Algebra F K] : omega F = omega K`; here because rank conditions are polynomial equations with coefficients in the prime field). Then, for an arbitrary `F`, take `p` with `CharP F p` (`CharP.exists`), split on `CharP.char_is_prime_or_zero`, install `ZMod.algebra F p` or (char 0) `CharP.charP_to_charZero` and the ℚ-algebra, and rewrite. This also lifts a result proved only for `k : Type` to all universes (`upper_of_small`). Conversely, a strict inequality over `F` is witnessed by a finite system and thus specialises to some `ZMod p` (`prime_specialization`). The final ω theorem is literally `contact_of_installations (fun p _ => Rounds.installable (ZMod p)) F`.
lean:
theorem upper_of_small {s : ℝ} (h : ∀ (k : Type) [Field k], omega k ≤ s)
    (F : Type*) [Field F] : omega F ≤ s := by
  obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := CharP.exists F
  rcases CharP.char_is_prime_or_zero F p with hprime | rfl
  · have : Fact p.Prime := ⟨hprime⟩
    let : Algebra (ZMod p) F := ZMod.algebra F p
    rw [omega_extension (ZMod p) F]
    exact h _
  · let : CharZero F := CharP.charP_to_charZero F
    rw [omega_extension ℚ F]
    exact h _

title: Lower-bound circuit cost by tensor rank via bilinearisation
problem: Lower bounds on arithmetic circuits (with additions, subtractions, even divisions) need an algebraic invariant that every gate can increase only a little.
method_md: The repo proves `tensorRank (matrixTensor F b c a) ≤ 2 * P.cost` for any formally correct program: track, for each wire, the matrix of mixed second partial derivatives in a left and a right variable; a multiplication gate adds at most two outer products, additions add none. It works in the rational function field (`FractionRing (MvPolynomial _ F)`) so divisions never require choosing a regular point, and the doc-string notes this "also avoids polarization in characteristic two". Once cost ≥ rank/2, exponent statements reduce to rank statements, where Strassen-style block recursion and asymptotic-rank arguments are available. Rank decompositions are stated as coefficient equations `∑ i, a i x * b i y * c i z = if … then 1 else 0` (`RankLE`), which are easy to specialise.
lean:
/-- Coefficient equations for a rank decomposition. The last index is an
output position (row of the left input, column of the right input). -/
def RankLE (F : Type*) [Field F] (n r : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b c : Fin r → Pos n → F, ∀ x y z : Pos n,
    ∑ i : Fin r, a i x * b i y * c i z =
      if x.1 = z.1 ∧ x.2 = y.1 ∧ y.2 = z.2 then 1 else 0

theorem matrixTensor_rank_le_twice_cost {a b c : ℕ} {P : MatrixAlgorithm F a b c}
    (h : FormalCorrect P) : tensorRank (matrixTensor F b c a) ≤ 2 * P.cost :=
  (matrixTensor_rank_le_twice_multiplicationCount h).trans
    (Nat.mul_le_mul_left 2 (multiplicationCount_le_cost _))

title: Normalise a symmetric max/min formula with split_ifs and grind
problem: A formula stated for sorted weights x ≥ y ≥ z must be matched against an internal function defined by cases on the order of a, b, c.
method_md: Name the sorted values with `let x := max a (max b c)`, `z := min …`, `y := a + b + c - x - z`, reduce the goal with `change` to the internal benchmark at (x, y, z), prove once that the benchmark is symmetric in its first two arguments (a `simp only` with `add_comm`, `mul_comm` and one `ring` fact), and then `unfold` the case definition and run `split_ifs <;> apply sorted <;> dsimp only [x, y, z] <;> grind`. `grind` closes the dozens of order side-conditions (which of a, b, c is max/min) that would otherwise each need `max_eq_left`/`min_eq_right` bookkeeping. The ω development uses `grind` only 68 times in 592 files, always for such finite order/arith case splits.
lean:
private theorem benchmark_sorted (a b c : ℝ) :
    U c b a =
      let x := max a (max b c)
      let z := min a (min b c)
      let y := a + b + c - x - z
      x + y + (max ((x + y) * z - x * y) 0) ^ 2 / (4 * x * y * z) := by
  let x := max a (max b c)
  let z := min a (min b c)
  let y := a + b + c - x - z
  change U c b a = benchmark x y z
  have sorted (u v w : ℝ) (hw : w = z)
      (huv : (u = x ∧ v = y) ∨ (u = y ∧ v = x)) :
      benchmark u v w = benchmark x y z := by
    rcases huv with ⟨hu, hv⟩ | ⟨hu, hv⟩ <;> rw [hu, hv, hw]
    simp only [benchmark, add_comm y x, mul_comm y x,
      show 4 * y * x = 4 * x * y by ring]
  unfold U
  split_ifs <;> apply sorted <;> dsimp only [x, y, z] <;> grind

title: Check whether a forced-PDE statement lets the force absorb the equation
problem: A statement asks for a solution of a forced equation (Navier–Stokes with force f) with extra properties; if f is free, any smooth u solves the equation with f := residual.
method_md: openai/math's Navier–Stokes computation theorem uses exactly this: pressure 0 and `f = f₀ + ν f₁` with `f₀ = inertialCoefficient U = ∂ₜU + (U·∇)U` and `f₁ = viscousCoefficient U = -ΔU`, so `ZeroDataSolution ν f U 0` holds by construction. The whole content is elsewhere: U divergence free and zero at t = 0, smoothness and bounded mixed derivatives of U and f, common compact support, periodicity after time 1, effectivity (computable rational approximations) of U, f₀, f₁, uniqueness in an energy class, and the halting equivalence for a particle trajectory. When a formal-conjectures style statement involves a forced PDE, first ask what constrains the force; if nothing does, the existence part is trivial and the real target is the side conditions. Conversely, when you prove such a statement, define the force as the residual and spend the effort on regularity and uniqueness.

def inertialCoefficient (u : Velocity) : Velocity :=
  fun t x => timeD u t x + convection u t x

def viscousCoefficient (u : Velocity) : Velocity :=
  fun t x => -laplacian u t x

def affineForce (f₀ f₁ : Velocity) (ν : ℝ) : Velocity :=
  fun t x => f₀ t x + ν • f₁ t x

def ZeroDataSolution (ν : ℝ) (f u : Velocity) (p : Pressure) : Prop :=
  Smooth u ∧ Smooth p ∧
  (∀ x, u 0 x = 0) ∧
  (∀ t, 0 ≤ t → ∀ x, div u t x = 0) ∧

    timeD u t x + convection u t x =

title: Prove uniqueness by an energy inequality and Mathlib's Gronwall bound
problem: Uniqueness of PDE solutions in a regularity class: the difference w = u − U has w(0) = 0 and an energy estimate dE/dt ≤ K E; one needs E ≡ 0 formally.
method_md: Represent the difference as an `Lp`-valued curve `V : ℝ → Lp Space 2 volume` with `HasDerivWithinAt V (W t) (Ici 0) t`, define `l2Energy V = ∑ i, ‖coordinateL2 i V‖^2` and its rate `2 * ∑ i, ⟪coord V, coord W⟫`, and get the derivative from `HasDerivWithinAt.norm_sq` summed with `HasDerivWithinAt.fun_sum`. Then apply `le_gronwallBound_of_liminf_deriv_right_le` with ε = 0 and initial value ≤ 0, rewrite with `gronwallBound_ε0_δ0` and conclude by `le_antisymm` with nonnegativity. The PDE work is only the pointwise bound `rate ≤ K * energy` on `Ico 0 T`, obtained by integration by parts on the convection term. Finally a continuous representative with zero L² energy is identically zero.
lean:
lemma l2Energy_eq_zero_of_bound
    {V W : ℝ → Lp Space 2 (volume : Measure Space)}
    (hV : ContinuousOn V (Ici 0))
    (hderiv : ∀ t, 0 ≤ t → HasDerivWithinAt V (W t) (Ici 0) t)
    (hzero : V 0 = 0) {T K : ℝ} (hT : 0 ≤ T)
    (hbound : ∀ t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) T, l2EnergyRate (V t) (W t) ≤ K * l2Energy (V t)) :
    l2Energy (V T) = 0 := by
  have hec : ContinuousOn (fun t => l2Energy (V t)) (Icc 0 T) :=
    l2Energy_continuous.comp_continuousOn (hV.mono (fun _ ht => ht.1))
  have he0 : l2Energy (V 0) ≤ 0 := by simp [hzero, l2Energy]
  have he' : ∀ x ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) T, ∀ r : ℝ, l2EnergyRate (V x) (W x) < r →
      ∃ᶠ z in 𝓝[>] x, (z-x)⁻¹ * (l2Energy (V z) - l2Energy (V x)) < r := by
    intro x hx r hr
    have hh : HasDerivWithinAt (fun t => l2Energy (V t))
        (l2EnergyRate (V x) (W x)) (Ici x) x :=
      (l2Energy_hasDerivWithinAt (hderiv x hx.1)).mono (Ici_subset_Ici.mpr hx.1)
    simpa only [slope_def_field, vsub_eq_sub, smul_eq_mul, div_eq_mul_inv, mul_comm]
      using hh.liminf_right_slope_le hr
  have H := le_gronwallBound_of_liminf_deriv_right_le (K := K) (ε := 0) hec he' he0
    (fun t ht => by simpa only [add_zero] using hbound t ht) T ⟨hT, le_rfl⟩
  rw [gronwallBound_ε0_δ0] at H
  exact le_antisymm H (l2Energy_nonneg _)

title: Encode C_t H^k regularity as continuous Lp-valued curves a.e. equal to the field
problem: Mathlib has no ready Bochner–Sobolev spaces C([0,∞); H^k); statements and uniqueness proofs still need "u ∈ C_t H²_x ∩ C¹_t L²_x".
method_md: Define the class directly: `CH k v` says for every list `a` of at most k spatial directions there is `V : ℝ → Lp F 2 volume`, continuous on `Ici 0`, with `V t =ᵐ spatialD a v t`; `C1L2 v` adds a second curve `W` that is the `HasDerivWithinAt` derivative of `V` on `Ici 0` and is a.e. the classical time derivative. Derivatives are classical (`fderiv` applied to `Pi.single i 1`), so smooth fields need no weak-derivative theory, while the Hilbert-space structure of `Lp` gives inner products and norms for energy arguments. Coordinates are extracted by `ContinuousLinearMap.compLpL 2 volume (ContinuousLinearMap.proj i)`, whose coercion lemma `coeFn_compLpL` gives the a.e. identity. This is a cheap, honest substitute for Sobolev spaces when all fields involved are smooth.
lean:
def CH (k : ℕ) (v : Field F) : Prop :=
  ∀ a : List (Fin 3), a.length ≤ k →
    ∃ V : ℝ → Lp F 2 (volume : Measure Space),
      ContinuousOn V (Set.Ici 0) ∧
      ∀ t, 0 ≤ t → (V t : Space → F) =ᵐ[volume] spatialD a v t

def C1L2 (v : Field F) : Prop :=
  ∃ V W : ℝ → Lp F 2 (volume : Measure Space),
    ContinuousOn V (Set.Ici 0) ∧ ContinuousOn W (Set.Ici 0) ∧
    ∀ t, 0 ≤ t →
      (V t : Space → F) =ᵐ[volume] v t ∧
      (W t : Space → F) =ᵐ[volume] timeD v t ∧
      HasDerivWithinAt V (W t) (Set.Ici 0) t

def coordinateL2 (i : Fin 3) :
    Lp Space 2 (volume : Measure Space) →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 (volume : Measure Space) :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.compLpL 2 volume (ContinuousLinearMap.proj i)

title: Integrate by parts on ℝ³ with only integrability hypotheses
problem: Energy estimates need ∫ f ∂ⱼg = −∫ ∂ⱼf g on the whole space without compact support, and the transport identity 2∫ a (∂w) w = −∫ (∂a) w².
method_md: Use `integral_mul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_mul_of_integrable`: it needs integrability of `∂f·g`, `f·∂g` and `f·g` plus differentiability, no decay assumption.     {p q : α → Prop} [DecidablePred p] [DecidablePred q]
    (hp : Computable fun a => decide (p a)) (hq : Computable fun a => decide (q a)) :

  exact (Computable.cond hp hq (Computable.const false)).of_eq (fun a => by

title: State effectivity of real fields with dyadic rational names
problem: Mathlib has no computable-real type; a statement that a real-valued field is "effective" needs a precise, checkable formulation.
method_md: Use names: `RealName name x := ∀ n, |(name n : ℝ) - x| ≤ (1/2)^n` with `name : ℕ → ℚ`, and `ComputableReal x := ∃ name, Computable name ∧ RealName name x`. A field is effective when one computable function `E : MultiIndex × ℚ-point × ℕ → (Fin 3 → ℚ)` approximates every mixed derivative at every rational space-time point to 2^-n, together with computable integer bounds `b a` on each derivative (and a computable support radius). Relative computability uses `ComputableIn {nameOracle name}` with `nameOracle name n := Part.some (encode (name n))`. Bundling the bounds into the definition is what makes later compositions (sums, products, gluing) effective without re-deriving moduli.
lean:
def error (n : ℕ) : ℝ := (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ ^ n

def RealName (name : ℕ → ℚ) (x : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ n, |(name n : ℝ) - x| ≤ error n

def ComputableReal (x : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ name : ℕ → ℚ, Computable name ∧ RealName name x

def nameOracle (name : ℕ → ℚ) : ℕ →. ℕ :=
  fun n => Part.some (Encodable.encode (name n))

def EffectiveFieldIn (O : Set (ℕ →. ℕ)) (v : Velocity) : Prop :=
  ∃ E : (MultiIndex × RationalPoint × ℕ) → (Fin 3 → ℚ),
  ∃ b : MultiIndex → ℕ,
    ComputableIn O E ∧ ComputableIn O b ∧
    (∀ a z n, 0 ≤ z.1 → ∀ i,
      |(E (a, z, n) i : ℝ) - mixedD a v (z.1 : ℝ) (rationalSpace z.2) i| ≤ error n) ∧
    (∀ a t, 0 ≤ t → ∀ x, ‖mixedD a v t x‖ ≤ (b a : ℝ))

title: Forced 3D Navier–Stokes flows from rest whose fixed particle detects Turing-machine halting

title: VP ≠ VNP over every field (exact binary-gate circuits)
problem: For each field F, the classes of polynomial families (variables Fin n × Bool at index n) computable by polynomial-size exact circuits (binary +, −, × with free variables and constants), and those obtained by summing a VP verifier over polynomially many Boolean witnesses, are different. Arity and degree are polynomially bounded in both.
method_md: Full Lean proof. The headline is a transport (`Standalone.vp_ne_vnp`) through `Valiant.Project.isVP_iff`/`isVNP_iff` to the internal `VPVNP.vp_ne_vnp`, which is `vp_ne_vnp_of_uniform_P separation_lower_bound F`. The lower bound is for state sums on square grids (via Euclidean tensor prices), and the same machinery gives `corollary12` (Hamiltonian cycle for all characteristics, permanent outside characteristic 2). The separate ArithmeticHierarchy challenge proves VF ⊊ VBP ⊊ VP ⊊ VNP. The import closure is 3,189 project files and 476k lines. It depends on external packages Lemmata, complexitylib and cslib besides Mathlib. Profile: simp ≈16.8k, omega ≈12.4k, decide ≈4.6k, bound ≈2.6k, 389 maxHeartbeats settings, 133 `irreducible` markers. The docs say that the explicit n^Ω((log n)^{1/12}) grid bound remains unformalized; only super-polynomial is proved.
lean:
def Computes {F σ : Type*} [Field F] (s : ℕ) (p : MvPolynomial σ F) : Prop :=
  ∃ v : Fin s → MvPolynomial σ F,
    let available (k : ℕ) (x : MvPolynomial σ F) :=
      (∃ j : σ, MvPolynomial.X j = x) ∨ (∃ a : F, MvPolynomial.C a = x) ∨
        ∃ j : Fin s, j.val < k ∧ v j = x
    available s p ∧ ∀ i : Fin s, ∃ a b, available i.val a ∧ available i.val b ∧
      (v i = a + b ∨ v i = a - b ∨ v i = a * b)

def IsVP (p : Family F σ) : Prop :=
  PFamily p ∧ ∃ s : ℕ → ℕ, PolynomiallyBounded s ∧ ∀ n, Computes (s n) (p n)

def IsVNP (p : Family F σ) : Prop :=
  PFamily p ∧ ∃ (W : ℕ → Type) (inst : ∀ n, Fintype (W n)) (g : Family F (fun n => σ n ⊕ W n)),
    PolynomiallyBounded (fun n => @Fintype.card _ (inst n)) ∧ IsVP g ∧ ∀ n,
      p n = ∑ y : W n → Bool, MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom MvPolynomial.C
        (Sum.elim MvPolynomial.X (fun i => MvPolynomial.C (if y i then 1 else 0))) (g n)

theorem vp_ne_vnp (F : Type u) [Field F] :
    (Valiant.Project.IsVP : Valiant.Project.Family F (fun n => Fin n × Bool) → Prop) ≠
      Valiant.Project.IsVNP := by

title: A finite counterexample to Sidorenko's conjecture (35-vertex bipartite pattern)
problem: Let H be the point–triple incidence graph of 22 explicit triples on 13 points (35 vertices, 66 edges). There is a finite simple graph G with an edge such that the homomorphism density t(H,G) is less than edgeDensity(G)^66 (homomorphisms include non-injective maps).
method_md: Full Lean proof, compact: 35 files, 24k lines, Mathlib only, no heartbeat settings. A symmetric counter-kernel is built and verified (`exists_symmetric_kernel`: orbits, signs, moments, coercivity, refinement histograms checked with `decide +kernel`; about 544 decide calls). `finiteHost_main` then samples a finite host by a first-moment argument, with collision error over 595 vertex pairs. The structure is a good template for "kernel counterexample → finite graph" proofs.

def H : SimpleGraph PatternVertex where
  Adj := incidence
  symm.symm := by intro left right; cases left <;> cases right <;> simp [incidence]
  loopless.irrefl := by intro vertex; cases vertex <;> simp [incidence]

noncomputable def homCount {V W : Type*} (F : SimpleGraph V) (G : SimpleGraph W) : ℕ :=
  Nat.card {hom : V → W // ∀ left right, F.Adj left right → G.Adj (hom left) (hom right)}

noncomputable def homDensity {V W : Type*} (F : SimpleGraph V) (G : SimpleGraph W) : ℝ :=
  (homCount F G : ℝ) / (Nat.card W : ℝ) ^ Nat.card V

noncomputable def edgeDensity {W : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph W) : ℝ :=
  2 * (Nat.card G.edgeSet : ℝ) / (Nat.card W : ℝ) ^ 2

/-- A finite simple host with at least one edge violates Sidorenko's inequality. -/
theorem main : ∃ size : ℕ, 0 < size ∧ ∃ host : SimpleGraph (Fin size),
    (∃ left right, host.Adj left right) ∧ homDensity H host < (edgeDensity host) ^ 66 := by

title: Rank-one projectors of ℝ⁴ give a Borsuk counterexample in dimension 9

title: Matrix multiplication tensor rank is at most twice the division-free circuit cost
problem: Reusable intermediate result: for a formally correct division-free program P multiplying a×b by b×c matrices over a field, tensorRank(matrixTensor F b c a) ≤ 2 · cost(P).

This is the standard bridge from cost lower bounds to rank lower bounds (Strassen), proved formally and without characteristic assumptions.

  (matrixTensor_rank_le_twice_multiplicationCount h).trans
    (Nat.mul_le_mul_left 2 (multiplicationCount_le_cost _))
